findings.title: Daily job reports success on every failure path: rejected calibrations, SPX download failure and hidden freeze warnings raise no alert
findings.description: main() ignores the return values of recalibrate_heston() and extend_regime_labels(). The only non-zero exit comes from freeze_site. Two consequences follow. (1) A rejected or failed calibration is logged at WARNING and the run is still green. GitHub only emails the person who last edited the cron when a scheduled run FAILS, so a successful run with a rejected calibration sends nobody a notification. That is how the site kept showing 'Calibration: 2026-09-11' for 9 sessions without anyone noticing. (2) An empty SPX download sets market_ok=False, and the script logs 'continuing with existing DB' and then labels, calibrates and publishes anyway. In CI the 'existing DB' is the committed one, whose SPX series ends 2026-06-18 (see ops-db-not-persisted). So one Yahoo failure publishes three-month-old market data as the current close, and the run still reports success. The script also writes the live option chain into the DB under the stale session date. Freeze stderr (sklearn/xgboost version warnings) is thrown away whenever the freeze succeeds. No run summary, annotations or artifacts are produced.
findings.evidence: GitHub API: runs 80-92 of 'Daily Market Refresh' (09-07..09-23) all have conclusion=success. git log shows exactly one pkl added since 09-05 (ad77c5b, joint_cal_2026-09-11.pkl). Run 35936484677 log: '00:04:29 WARNING Calibration REJECTED (SPX RMSE too high (175.97vp > 3.0))' then 'Refresh complete', job success. Failure simulation in a private copy (download_spx_ohlcv monkeypatched to return an empty frame): 'market_ok = False', then '[3/4] Downloading SPX options for session 2026-06-18 (run date 2026-09-24)', 'Saved 3458 option contracts as the 2026-06-18 SPX snapshot', 'SPX spot S = 7500.58 (date: 2026-06-18)'. The fit (SPX RMSE 0.37vp) was rejected only because the committed 2026-06-20 snapshot happened to postdate the stale session ('SPX surface is stale (snapshot 2026-06-20, session 2026-06-18)'). The script still exits 0. Freezing the committed repo state renders 'Last close: 2026-06-18', where the live site shows 'Last close: 2026-09-23'.
findings.proposed_fix: Make main() return an explicit status. Exit non-zero (fail the job) when the SPX download is empty after retries, when the expected NYSE session (from exchange_calendars or pandas_market_calendars) is missing from the DB, or when the latest accepted calibration is more than N sessions old (for example N=3). Always write a Markdown run summary to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (session, rows per source, calibration accepted or rejected with reason, headline calibration date and age). Emit '::warning::'/'::error::' annotations. Add a step `if: failure()` that opens or updates a GitHub issue with `gh issue create`. Log freeze stderr on success as well. Add a pre-deploy freshness assertion on the frozen HTML (last close == session, calibration age <= N). Test: monkeypatch download_spx_ohlcv to return empty and assert SystemExit != 0. Set the calibration age to more than N and assert the job fails or the summary contains the warning.

findings.title: vol_system.db is tracked but the bot never commits it: captured data is lost, a Yahoo gap is published as a daily move, clean clones render June data, and a time bomb is set for 2027-07-28
findings.description: The workflow comment says 'The SQLite DB is NOT committed (binary bloat — rebuilt fresh each run)'. Both halves are false. data_store/vol_system.db (11.6 MB) is tracked, and each run starts from that committed copy (SPX/VIX/term structure end 2026-06-18) plus a 400-day Yahoo overlay. The bot then discards the DB. Consequences: (a) the daily SPX option chain (2,206 rows on 09-23) is thrown away every day. The README still lists 'single-snapshot options' as a key limitation while the bot fetches, and drops, a chain every day. (b) Yahoo history can be revised, and anything the bot captured but Yahoo later drops is gone for good. The 09-22 run stored a 2026-09-22 row in regime_labels.parquet (vix=0.1421), but Yahoo no longer has a 09-22 ^GSPC/^VIX bar. The 09-24 run's DB therefore lacked 09-22, and the live site's 'SPX −0.76%' for 09-23 is really the two-session change 09-21 → 09-23. The 09-23 regime features were also computed on a series with that gap. (c) A clean clone, the Procfile deployment and redeploy_site.sh all render 'Last close 2026-06-18'. (d) The fetch window is today−400d. Once today−400d is later than 2026-06-22 (from run date 2027-07-28), a gap opens between the committed DB and the download. Labels in the 252-day adaptive window over that gap are recomputed wrongly, and the self-heal step overwrites the stored labels with them.
findings.evidence: `git ls-files data_store` lists data_store/vol_system.db (11,664 KB). The workflow's git add covers only regime_labels.parquet and joint_cal_*.pkl. Committed DB: spx_ohlcv max(date)=2026-06-18, options_snapshots last=2026-06-20. Yahoo now: `yf.Ticker('^GSPC').history('2026-09-17','2026-09-25')` → 09-17, 09-18, 09-21, 09-23 (no 09-22). history(2025-08-20..2026-09-23) = 274 rows against 275 NYSE sessions (286 weekdays minus 11 holidays). The 09-24 CI log also says 'Downloaded 274 SPX OHLCV rows'. regime_labels.parquet tail includes 2026-09-22. app.py:154-160 takes the change from the last two DB rows: 7706.03/7764.70−1 = −0.7556%, which the live site shows as −0.76%. Local freeze of HEAD bddbbec vs live: 36 differing lines on index, including '-Last close: 2026-06-18 / +Last close: 2026-09-23'. Date arithmetic: 2026-06-22 + 400 days = 2027-07-27. One option snapshot (17,451 rows) is 336 KB as zstd parquet.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the raw captures as the source of truth in git and treat the DB as a rebuildable cache. Each run should append the day's rows to data_store/daily/{spx_ohlcv,vix_daily,vix_ts,tbill}.parquet and write data_store/options/spx_<session>.parquet (about 50-350 KB per day), then commit them alongside the labels and pkl. At the start of each run, rebuild or upsert the DB from those files plus a download window that starts at min(today−400d, last_persisted_date−10d), so no gap can open. Make upserts never delete a row Yahoo has dropped, and log a warning when the download is missing a session that is stored. Alternatively, commit vol_system.db itself with `git add` (simplest, but about 11 MB of binary history per day). Correct the workflow comment and README. Tests: (1) run twice with a mocked Yahoo that drops a session on the second run, and assert the session survives and spx_chg uses the true previous session; (2) set TODAY=2027-09-01 against the committed DB and assert no date gap in get_spx_ohlcv.

findings.title: The C21 'rule labels, not classifier' fix is incomplete: `python dashboard/app.py` rewrites the tracked regime_labels.parquet with demoted-classifier predictions
findings.description: Commit 90dc851 stopped the bot from appending clf.predict output to regime_labels.parquet. app.py still has its own `_refresh_regime_labels()`, which loads regime_classifier.pkl, calls `clf.predict_series(feats.dropna())` and overwrites the whole parquet (a tracked file). The README's documented local run command (`python dashboard/app.py`) starts `_startup_data_refresh` in a thread. On a clean clone the committed DB is always more than 3 days stale, so it always runs DataPipeline.daily_refresh() and then `_refresh_regime_labels()`. DataPipeline downloads only the last 5 days, which also leaves a three-month hole in the DB. The result is a dirty working tree containing corrupted labels, one `git commit -a` or `./redeploy_site.sh` away from being published. The bot's self-heal only repairs the last ~370 sessions (>= safe_from), so older corrupted rows would never be fixed.
findings.evidence: In a private copy: `mod._startup_data_refresh()` logged 'Stale data: last SPX=2026-06-18 … spx_ohlcv +2 rows … regime_labels.parquet updated: 4088 rows, last date 2026-06-18'. Before: 4,189 rows to 2026-09-23. After: 4,088 rows to 2026-06-18. 1,320 of 4,088 common labels changed (32.3%), 1,254 of them on or before 2025-03-24 (inside the backtest window). `git status` afterwards: ' M data_store/signals/regime_labels.parquet', ' M data_store/vol_system.db'.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete app.py's `_refresh_regime_labels`, or replace its body with a call to the same rule-based `extend_regime_labels` used by cloud_refresh (move it into a library module, e.g. joint_vol_calibration/signals/label_store.py). Gate the startup and scheduled refresh threads behind an explicit env flag (VOL_LIVE_REFRESH=1, off by default), and never let the web process write tracked artifacts. Make DataPipeline.daily_refresh start from the DB's last date, not today−5d. Test: import app, call `_startup_data_refresh()` with network mocked, and assert regime_labels.parquet is byte-identical, or that its labels still equal build_regime_labels(vvix_threshold=None). Extend test_c21_audit_fixes to grep app.py for `predict_series` writes to regime_labels.parquet.

findings.title: Daily job downloads 3.47 GB every run (3.35 GB is CUDA torch/NCCL); torch is imported only for a numpy helper, and the pip cache is frozen and shared
findings.description: The daily job runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` with `torch>=2.0.0` from PyPI, which pulls the full CUDA 13 stack. xgboost pulls nvidia-nccl-cu12 (351.5 MB). Install takes 117 s of a 167 s job, and cloud_refresh itself takes 24 s. torch is only needed because risk_monitor.py:80 imports `_bs_iv_vectorized` from nn_pricer, which runs `import torch` at module level, even though `_bs_iv_vectorized` is pure numpy. Nothing else in the daily path uses torch; it is first imported when the /backtest page renders. The actions/cache key `${runner.os}-pip-${hashFiles('requirements.txt')}` is identical in tests.yml (CPU torch) and daily_refresh.yml (CUDA torch). Because requirements.txt never changes, the key always hits ('Cache hit occurred on the primary key … not saving cache'), so the 1,055 MB cache is frozen at its first save while pip floats forward. The cache restores 1 GB and still downloads 3.47 GB.
findings.evidence: Run 35936484677 step timings: Install dependencies 00:02:12 → 00:04:09 (117 s), Run cloud_refresh.py 00:04:09 → 00:04:33. Parsing the log's 'Downloading … (N MB)' lines gives 3,468 MB total, of which 3,351 MB is torch/nvidia/cuda/triton: torch-2.14.0 554.6, cudnn 553.1, cublas 423.1, nccl_cu12 351.5, triton 247.9 … 'Cache Size: ~1055 MB'. Import trace: torch absent from sys.modules after rendering '/', '/calibration' and '/greeks'. First import at risk_monitor.py:80 while rendering /backtest. Wheel sizes: torch-2.14.0+cpu = 196 MB; xgboost_cpu-3.2.0 = 5.6 MB (no NCCL dependency).
findings.proposed_fix: Move `_bs_iv_vectorized` (and any other numpy helpers) to joint_vol_calibration/models/bs_utils.py and import it from both modules, or lazy-import torch inside NNPricer. Split dependencies into requirements.txt (runtime: no torch) and requirements-ml.txt (torch, installed from https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu in tests.yml only). Use `xgboost-cpu; sys_platform == 'linux'` in CI. Replace the manual actions/cache step with `actions/setup-python@v6` `cache: pip` plus `cache-dependency-path` pointing at a hashed lock file (see ops-no-lockfile), or with astral-sh/setup-uv, which keys on the lock and Python version. Expected result: install under 20 s and about 120 MB downloaded. Test: `python -X importtime scripts/cloud_refresh.py` or `python -c 'import dashboard freeze; assert "torch" not in sys.modules'` after rendering all four routes.

findings.title: Floor-only requirements with no lock: the bot publishes the site from a dependency set CI never tested, and unpickles sklearn 1.7.1 / old-xgboost models under newer versions
findings.description: Every requirement is a `>=` floor (pandas>=2.0.0 already admits a major version, pandas 3). Each daily run resolves the newest wheels, so the environment that renders the public site changes silently from day to day. The last CI test run (09-05) resolved pandas 3.0.5 and scikit-learn 1.9.0. The 09-23 daily run used pandas 3.0.6 and scikit-learn 1.9.1, a combination no test has seen. The dashboard unpickles regime_classifier.pkl, built with sklearn 1.7.1 and an older xgboost, and emits InconsistentVersionWarning for FrozenEstimator, IsotonicRegression and CalibratedClassifierCV, plus the xgboost 'serialized model generated by an older version' warning. A future sklearn or xgboost release that breaks unpickling will stop the daily deploy (freeze exits 1), or will change the displayed classifier probabilities with no signal. There is no Dependabot or Renovate config to move versions deliberately.
findings.evidence: Daily log 09-24 'Successfully installed … pandas-3.0.6 … scikit-learn-1.9.1 … torch-2.14.0 … xgboost-3.2.0 yfinance-1.7.0'. tests log 09-05: 'pandas-3.0.5 … scikit-learn-1.9.0'. The tests log warnings summary contains 'InconsistentVersionWarning: Trying to unpickle estimator CalibratedClassifierCV from version 1.7.1 when using version 1.9.0' (×13 each) and the xgboost 'older version of XGBoost' UserWarning. The local run printed the same warnings under 1.9.1. `git ls-files` shows no lock, pyproject or .github/dependabot.yml.
findings.proposed_fix: Generate a hashed lock (`uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.lock --generate-hashes`, or pip-compile). Install from it in both workflows with `--require-hashes`, and keep requirements.in with compatible ranges (pandas>=2.2,<4 and so on). Add .github/dependabot.yml for pip and github-actions (weekly), so upgrades arrive as PRs that tests.yml gates. Re-export the classifier with `booster.save_model('regime_xgb.json')` and the calibrator with skops, or retrain under the locked versions, and make CI fail on InconsistentVersionWarning (`-W error::sklearn.exceptions.InconsistentVersionWarning`). Add a weekly `schedule:` trigger to tests.yml to catch drift. Test: run CI with the lock; `pip install --dry-run -r requirements.lock` must be a no-op between runs.

findings.title: Nothing tests what gets published: bot pushes never trigger tests.yml, the daily job runs no tests, and CI never exercises freeze_site
findings.description: The README says 'Every push to main runs the full suite in GitHub Actions … so passing is machine-verified'. Pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger other workflows, so none of the 12 bot pushes since 09-05 was tested. The CI badge still reflects the 09-05 run. The daily job has no pytest or smoke step before committing and deploying. tests.yml never renders the dashboard or runs freeze_site, so a template or render regression is first detected by the production deploy, and only if it raises a Traceback or returns non-200.
findings.evidence: GitHub API: tests.yml total_count=18, latest run 33963976076 at 2026-09-05T11:40Z. Since then there are 12 bot commits on main (bd666a8 … bddbbec) and no tests runs. `grep -rn 'freeze_site\|test_client' joint_vol_calibration/tests` finds no dashboard render test. freeze_site succeeds offline in a private copy (4× 'OK … status=200'), so it can run in CI.
findings.proposed_fix: In daily_refresh.yml, add a step before the commit step: `pytest -q -m 'smoke' joint_vol_calibration/tests` (tag the data-pipeline, label-provenance and gate tests) plus a freshness assertion on .site-build. In tests.yml, add `python dashboard/freeze_site.py "$RUNNER_TEMP/site"` and upload the result with actions/upload-artifact, so every PR shows the rendered site. Add `schedule: - cron: '41 6 * * 1'` to tests.yml. Reword the README sentence to 'every human push and PR' or make it true. Test: introduce a template error in a PR and confirm tests.yml fails.

findings.title: A contents:write GITHUB_TOKEN sits in .git/config while ~70 unpinned PyPI packages execute; third-party actions are unpinned
findings.description: actions/checkout keeps the default persist-credentials: true, so the contents:write token is stored as http.https://github.com/.extraheader in .git/config for the whole job. That includes `python scripts/cloud_refresh.py`, which imports yfinance, curl_cffi, xgboost, sklearn and their transitive dependencies, all floor-pinned and freshly resolved every day. A single compromised release of any of them can read the token and push to main or gh-pages. Actions are referenced by mutable tags, including the third-party peaceiris/actions-gh-pages, which receives the write token.
findings.evidence: zizmor 1.30.1 (--persona=auditor): 7× error[unpinned-uses] (checkout@v4, setup-python@v5, cache@v4, peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4), warning[artipacked] for both checkouts, error[excessive-permissions] daily_refresh.yml:24. Post-job log: 'git config --local --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader', which confirms the token was persisted until the end of the job. The run log shows 'GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions Contents: write'.
findings.proposed_fix: Split into jobs. Job `refresh` (permissions: contents: read; checkout with persist-credentials: false) runs cloud_refresh and uploads data files plus .site-build as artifacts. Job `publish` (contents: write) downloads them and commits and pushes with `git -c http.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic $(echo -n x-access-token:${{ github.token }} | base64)" push`. Job `deploy` uses actions/upload-pages-artifact + actions/deploy-pages (permissions: pages: write, id-token: write; environment: github-pages) instead of peaceiris and the gh-pages branch. Pin every action to a full commit SHA with a version comment (`pinact run`), and let Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem bump them. Test: zizmor --offline .github/workflows exits 0; actionlint passes.

findings.title: No concurrency group and no rebase on push: a push to main during the ~3-minute run rejects the bot's push, skips the deploy and loses that session's pkl
findings.description: The job checks out main at trigger time (fetch-depth 1) and later runs a plain `git push origin main`. The workflow has no `concurrency:` block, so workflow_dispatch and schedule runs can overlap, and human pushes land on main during runs (the author pushed several commits on 09-05 while bot runs were happening that day). A rejected push fails the step under bash -e, so the deploy is skipped. The session's accepted calibration pkl is then lost for good, because the next run calibrates the next session, and the day's labels are not committed.
findings.evidence: Local reproduction with a bare remote: the bot clone commits a data file after a human pushed → ' ! [rejected] main -> main (fetch first)' … 'step exit code=1'. zizmor: help[concurrency-limits] on both workflows.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `concurrency: { group: daily-refresh, cancel-in-progress: false }` to daily_refresh.yml, and `concurrency: { group: tests-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` to tests.yml. In the commit step: `for i in 1 2 3; do git pull --rebase --autostash origin main && git push origin main && break; sleep $((i*10)); done`. If the only conflicts are in bot-owned files, re-run the label merge rather than failing. Test: repeat the bare-remote simulation with the new script and assert the push succeeds.

findings.title: Commit and deploy messages are wrong: run-date instead of session date, 'Heston recalibration' when none happened, a literal '$(date -u …)', and the pre-refresh SHA
findings.description: The main-branch commit title uses `$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)` at commit time. Runs start 87-139 min after the 22:00 cron, so 3 of 13 runs crossed midnight. That produced two commits titled 2026-09-15 and two titled 2026-09-22, and 'Auto-refresh 2026-09-24' actually holds the 09-23 session. That undoes the session-naming fix from 236509e for the commit history. Every title says '+ Heston recalibration' although 11 of the 12 trading-session runs since 09-05 wrote no pkl. peaceiris does not shell-expand commit_message, so all 69 gh-pages commits literally read 'Deploy <run_id>: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) <sha>'. The SHA it appends is GITHUB_SHA, the pre-refresh commit (ef47f93), not the data commit the site was built from (bddbbec). The bot email lacks the numeric ID, so commits are not linked to the bot account.
findings.evidence: git log: e722eec 2026-09-22 00:21 'Auto-refresh 2026-09-22' (Monday 09-21 run) and ef47f93 2026-09-22 23:54 'Auto-refresh 2026-09-22'; 8d030a8 09-15 00:04 and 8ff4882 09-15 23:49; bddbbec 09-24 00:04 for session 09-23 (log: 'regime_labels now at 2026-09-23'). gh-pages: 83633b4 'Deploy 35936484677: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) ef47f936…' while the same log shows 'ef47f93..bddbbec main -> main'. `git rev-list --count gh-pages` = 69, all with the literal $(…).
findings.proposed_fix: Have cloud_refresh write `session=`, `calibration=accepted|rejected|skipped`, `reason=` and `labels_added=` to $GITHUB_OUTPUT (step id: refresh). Commit with `-m "Auto-refresh session ${SESSION}: labels +${N}; calibration ${STATUS}"`, and capture `sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` as an output. Use peaceiris `full_commit_message: "Deploy session ${{ steps.refresh.outputs.session }} from ${{ steps.commit.outputs.sha }} (run ${{ github.run_id }})"`, or with deploy-pages this becomes moot. Use `41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com`. Test: run workflow_dispatch after 00:00 UTC and check that the commit title shows the previous session.

findings.title: Cron at minute :00 is consistently 87-139 minutes late (the comment says 30-90) and has no catch-up slot if GitHub drops the run
findings.description: GitHub's docs say scheduled events are delayed at high load, 'High load times include the start of every hour', and 'some queued jobs may be dropped'. The schedule uses '0 22 * * 1-5', the worst possible minute. There is only one slot per day, so a dropped run means that session is never calibrated or labelled by the bot. The job is idempotent (it skips if the session pkl exists), so a second slot would be free insurance.
findings.evidence: created_at for runs 80-92 vs 22:00 UTC: 109, 103, 94, 87, 95, 122, 106, 115, 106, 100, 139, 113, 122 min (min 87, median 106, max 139). All 13 exceed the '30-90 min late' in the comment. Docs quote fetched from docs.github.com events-that-trigger-workflows#schedule.
findings.proposed_fix: Use an off-peak minute, for example `- cron: '23 22 * * 1-5'`, and add a catch-up slot `- cron: '47 1 * * 2-6'` (after midnight UTC, still well before the next open). Both are no-ops once the session pkl and labels exist, which requires the recalibrate skip and the label 'already current' path, both already present. Update the comment with the measured delays. Test: check run created_at deltas over a week.

findings.title: Workflow comment, README and substack say ^VIX9D/^VIX3M/^VIX6M have 'no history' on Yahoo; Yahoo and the committed DB both have full history, and the README cron time is stale
findings.description: The cron rationale ('must run … before Yahoo rolls that row … ~04:00 UTC … 6 h of slack') and the published postmortem both rest on the claim that the sub-tenor indices exist on Yahoo only as a current-day row. That is not true. The August outage is fully explained by the exclusive end date that 236509e fixed. The README also says the cron 'moved to 21:30 UTC', but it was later moved to 22:00 (90dc851).
findings.evidence: `yf.Ticker(t).history(start='2025-06-02', end='2026-09-25')` returns 329 rows for each of ^VIX9D, ^VIX3M, ^VIX6M and ^VVIX, the same as ^GSPC. The 09-24 CI log shows 'Downloaded 1372 VIX term structure rows (dates: 2025-08-20 to 2026-09-23)', which is 5 tickers × ~274 days. The committed DB has ^VIX9D rows from 2011-01-03 to 2026-06-18 (3,885 rows) sourced from Yahoo per the README's own data table. The cron line in the workflow is '0 22 * * 1-5'.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the comment and postmortem to cite only the exclusive-end bug. Drop the 04:00 UTC constraint, or restate it as 'run after the 16:15 ET settle'. Fix README:135-136 to say 22:00 UTC, or remove the time entirely and reference the workflow. Test: none needed. Optionally add a unit test asserting that download_vix_term_structure over a 30-day window returns more than one date per tenor (network-marked).

findings.title: redeploy_site.sh force-pushes an orphan gh-pages built from local (stale) data, wiping deploy history and overwriting the bot's site
findings.description: The script runs `git init` inside .site-build, `checkout -B gh-pages`, then `git push -f`. It replaces the bot-maintained gh-pages history with the local one, and it publishes whatever the local data_store renders. On a clean clone that is 'Last close: 2026-06-18' (see ops-db-not-persisted), or labels corrupted by app.py (see ops-app-refresh-overwrites-labels). It bypasses every CI gate, and its header ('It does not auto-update') has been false since the daily bot existed. The author name and email and the repo URL are hard-coded. The gh-pages root commit shows this has already happened once.
findings.evidence: Simulation against a bare copy of the real gh-pages branch, with the REPO line pointed at the copy: 'before: 69 commits on gh-pages' → ' + 83633b4...a315d42 gh-pages -> gh-pages (forced update)' → 'after: 1 commits on gh-pages'. The real gh-pages root commit is 7310708 'Deploy: 635 tests' by Navnoor Bawa, 2026-06-26, while the Pages build counter is at run 112, which shows earlier history was already wiped. shellcheck reports no issues; the hazard is in the logic.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete redeploy_site.sh. Or replace its body with `gh workflow run daily_refresh.yml --ref main && gh run watch`, so every deploy goes through the same gated pipeline, and add a `workflow_dispatch` input `skip_calibration: true` for pure re-renders. If a local deploy must stay, remove -f, fetch origin/gh-pages first, refuse to run when `git status --porcelain data_store` is non-empty, and read identity from git config. Test: rerun the bare-remote simulation and assert the gh-pages commit count increases by exactly 1.

findings.title: Every page declares canonical and og:url = https://navnoorbawa.me/, contradicting the sitemap; sitemap lastmod is bumped daily for pages that did not change
findings.description: base.html hard-codes `<link rel=canonical href=https://navnoorbawa.me/>` and `og:url` for all four pages. Search engines are told that calibration.html, greeks.html and backtest.html are duplicates of the home page, while the sitemap lists them as distinct canonical URLs. Shared links to a subpage also preview as the home page. All pages share one meta description. freeze_site stamps `lastmod=date.today()` on all four URLs every run, although calibration.html last changed on 09-11. Google ignores lastmod values that are consistently inaccurate.
findings.evidence: Live HTML: calibration.html, greeks.html and backtest.html each contain '<link rel="canonical" href="https://navnoorbawa.me/">' and 'og:url content="https://navnoorbawa.me/"'. Live sitemap.xml has lastmod 2026-09-24 for all 4 URLs. gh-pages diffs: 83633b4 changed only 'index.html sitemap.xml'; calibration.html last changed in 532c3b7 (09-11). The local freeze of HEAD vs live shows 0 differing lines for calibration, greeks and backtest.
findings.proposed_fix: In base.html, use `{% set canon = {'/':'', '/calibration':'calibration.html', '/greeks':'greeks.html', '/backtest':'backtest.html'}[request.path] %}`, emit `href="https://navnoorbawa.me/{{ canon }}"` for both canonical and og:url, and add a per-page `{% block description %}`. In freeze_site, compute lastmod per page from a content hash compared with the previously deployed page (fetch it or keep a manifest), or from the calibration and label dates that page depends on. Test: assert each frozen page's canonical equals its sitemap loc.

findings.title: checkout@v4, setup-python@v5 and cache@v4 still target Node 20 (removed from runners 2026-09-23); FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24 and its comment are stale
findings.description: Node 24 became the default on 2026-06-16 and Node 20 was removed on 2026-09-23, per the GitHub changelog. The three first-party actions still declare node20 and are force-run on Node 24, with a warning on every run. The env var comment ('opt-in ahead of June 16 cutover') describes a date that has passed. peaceiris@v4 already targets node24.
findings.evidence: Daily log 09-24: '##[warning]Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/cache@v4, actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-python@v5.' Changelog 2025-09-19: 'June 16, 2026: Node24 becomes default … September 23, 2026: Node20 is completely removed'. `git ls-remote --tags`: checkout v7.0.1, setup-python v7.0.0/v6.3.0, cache v6.1.0 are available. actionlint on both files: 0 errors.
findings.proposed_fix: Bump to actions/checkout@v5 or later, actions/setup-python@v6, and remove actions/cache in favour of setup-python's `cache: pip` (or cache@v5), all pinned by SHA (see ops-token-persisted). Delete FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24 and its comments. Add .github/dependabot.yml with the github-actions ecosystem. Test: the next run log has no 'Node.js 20 is deprecated' warning.

findings.title: Procfile/gunicorn deployment is dead config: under gunicorn the refresh threads in __main__ never start, so it would serve the June DB
findings.description: The site is GitHub Pages only. The repo has no Heroku, Railway, Render or Fly config besides the Procfile, yet app.py comments refer to Railway health checks. Under the Procfile's gunicorn command the module is imported as dashboard.app, so the startup and 4-hour refresh threads, which exist only in `if __name__ == '__main__'`, never run. A PaaS deploy would serve the committed DB (last close 2026-06-18) indefinitely. Starting those threads would be worse still, given ops-app-refresh-overwrites-labels. gunicorn is installed on every daily and CI run for nothing.
findings.evidence: `PORT=58123 gunicorn --chdir . dashboard.app:app …` returned 200 for / (1.5 s) and /backtest (2.2 s), with no 'Startup refresh thread launched' line in the gunicorn log. `git ls-files` contains no railway.json, render.yaml, fly.toml, app.json or runtime.txt.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete Procfile, drop gunicorn from requirements.txt, and remove the Railway comments. If a live server is wanted later, add a documented `create_app()` that starts no writers, and deploy it with a real config. Test: CI still green; `grep -rn gunicorn` finds nothing.

findings.title: Social card image says '631 tests'; og:image:alt and README say 666; CI says 642 passed + 24 skipped
findings.description: make_og_image.py hard-codes stats=('631','tests'), and the committed og-image.png (the card every LinkedIn, Twitter and Substack preview shows) renders '631 tests'. The alt text in base.html says '666 tests'. Nothing regenerates the image in CI, so it will drift again.
findings.evidence: Viewed dashboard/og-image.png: '14 components / 631 tests / 0 look-ahead / 2018–25 backtest'. The live index.html og:image:alt reads '… 14 components, 666 tests …'. The local pytest run gives '642 passed, 24 skipped'.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the test count from the card (it is not a stable fact), or have make_og_image read the count from a CI-produced file and regenerate the image inside freeze_site. Align the alt text. Test: a unit test asserting that the og-image stats and base.html alt contain the same number, or no number.

findings.title: The calibrator's print() output appears after 'Refresh complete' in CI logs (block-buffered stdout); freeze stderr is dropped on success
findings.description: logging writes to unbuffered stderr, while JointCalibrator uses print() to stdout, which is block-buffered when piped in Actions. The whole '[C4] Joint calibration … Loss Breakdown' block is therefore flushed at process exit, after '[4/4] Freezing' and 'Refresh complete'. Anyone debugging the outage reads the calibration details out of order and under the wrong step. The freeze subprocess's stderr, which carries the sklearn and xgboost version warnings, is only printed on failure.
findings.evidence: Run 35936484677: '00:04:29 WARNING Calibration REJECTED' → '00:04:33 INFO Refresh complete' → then '[C4] Joint calibration: 2026-09-24 … DE done … SPX smile RMSE : 175.97 vol pts', all stamped 00:04:33.72, although the fit ran 00:04:21-00:04:29.
findings.proposed_fix: Set `env: PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"` on the job, or run `python -u`. Replace print() in the calibrator with logging. In freeze_site(), always forward result.stderr at WARNING level. Wrap each stage in `::group::`/`::endgroup::` for readable logs. Test: log order matches stage order in the next run.

findings.title: cloud_refresh does os.chdir and logging.basicConfig at import, which makes 3 C21 tests pass or fail depending on test order and CWD
findings.description: Importing cloud_refresh (test_data_pipeline does) changes the pytest process's CWD to the repo root, configures root logging, and freezes TODAY at import time. test_c21_audit_fixes reads `pathlib.Path('scripts/cloud_refresh.py')` relative to the CWD, so its outcome depends on whether test_data_pipeline ran first. The same side effects make cloud_refresh awkward to reuse or test with a mocked date.
findings.evidence: From joint_vol_calibration/: `pytest tests/test_c21_audit_fixes.py` → '3 failed, 6 passed' (test_adaptive_gate_reproduces_shipped_labels, test_refresh_labels_with_rule_not_classifier, test_bot_writes_the_table_the_calibrator_reads). `pytest tests/test_data_pipeline.py tests/test_c21_audit_fixes.py` → '19 passed'.
findings.proposed_fix: Move os.chdir, logging.basicConfig and TODAY into a `main(today: date | None = None)` function called under `if __name__ == '__main__'`, and pass `today` through the steps. In the tests, resolve paths with `pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / 'scripts' / 'cloud_refresh.py'`. Test: run the test file on its own from any directory, and run with `-p random_order`.

findings.title: latest_session_date() claims 'most recent CLOSED session' but takes the last row without checking the NYSE close; a manual dispatch during market hours would permanently name a fit for an open session
findings.description: yfinance daily history includes today's in-progress bar during the regular session. workflow_dispatch is used in practice (runs 77 and 79). A dispatch between 13:30 and 20:15 UTC would therefore treat an intraday bar as a closed session. The script writes joint_cal_<today>.pkl from intraday spot and quotes, and that file is immutable because `if out.exists(): skip`. It also appends a regime-label row whose stored feature columns come from the intraday bar; the self-heal only repairs the 'regime' column.
findings.evidence: The code returns `str(spx_df['date'].iloc[-1])[:10]` with no time check. Synthetic check: latest_session_date(pd.DataFrame({'date':['2026-09-23','2026-09-24'],'close':[1,2]})) returns '2026-09-24' whatever the wall clock. The run list shows workflow_dispatch runs 77 (09-04 21:30Z) and 79 (09-05 11:37Z).
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the last row when its date equals today in America/New_York and now_ET < 16:15 (use exchange_calendars for early closes). Better, compute the expected last closed session from the calendar and require the DB to contain it. Add a unit test with a frozen clock at 14:00 ET that expects the previous session.

findings.title: tests.yml comment says '633 passed, 24 skipped' (actual 642); pytest-cov is installed but coverage never runs
findings.description: The hard-coded count has gone stale twice (610/18, then 633/24). pytest-cov adds install time without producing any coverage. The suite also emits 79 warnings, including a PytestRemovedIn10Warning that will become an error in pytest 10.
findings.evidence: Private-copy run: '642 passed, 24 skipped, 79 warnings in 67.65s'. CI run 33963976076: '642 passed, 24 skipped, 79 warnings'. Comment text: 'a clean CI checkout reports "633 passed, 24 skipped"'. There is no --cov flag anywhere.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the number with 'the NN tests skip without weights', or have CI write the summary to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY with `pytest -q --junitxml` plus a summary action. Either run `--cov=joint_vol_calibration --cov-report=xml` or drop pytest-cov. Fix the class-scoped fixtures flagged by PytestRemovedIn10Warning (test_delta_hedger, test_heston, test_joint_calibrator, test_regime_pdv). Test: `pytest -W error::pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning` passes.

findings.title: The published site loads Chart.js from jsDelivr with no Subresource Integrity and no local copy
findings.description: Every frozen page runs `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js@4.4.3/dist/chart.umd.min.js">` without integrity or crossorigin attributes. A CDN compromise could inject script into navnoorbawa.me, and a CDN outage blanks every chart. freeze_site already copies assets (og-image) and could serve the file locally instead.
findings.evidence: base.html:25 has no integrity attribute. Frozen pages contain the same tag.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `integrity="sha384-…" crossorigin="anonymous"` for the exact file, or vendor chart.umd.min.js into dashboard/static and have freeze_site copy it and rewrite the src. Test: the frozen HTML contains no third-party script without integrity (simple grep test).

checked_ok: actionlint (with shellcheck) reports 0 errors on both workflow files. yamllint (relaxed) reports only line-length and colon-spacing style warnings. shellcheck on redeploy_site.sh is clean.
A failed freeze does not half-deploy the site: freeze_site exits 1, cloud_refresh calls sys.exit(1), and the commit and deploy steps are skipped.

freeze_site link rewriting is complete. The frozen HTML has no root-relative href/src/action left and uses no fetch() or /api calls. The 404 page's absolute '/' link is correct for nested unknown paths.

Live hosting behaves correctly: http→https, www→apex and github.io/vol-system-dashboard→apex all return 301; an unknown path returns 404 with the branded page; CNAME, .nojekyll, robots.txt (valid, points to the sitemap) and a well-formed sitemap.xml are all served. Cache-Control is max-age=600.
peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4 already targets Node 24. force_orphan:false with keep_files:false keeps gh-pages history (69 commits) and removes stale files.
The DST arithmetic in the cron comment is right: 22:00 UTC is 105 min after the 16:15 ET settle under EDT and 45 min under EST.
Session-named pkls, the holiday path and idempotency are fine: the Labor Day run (09-07) produced no data commit, and the regime_labels.parquet write is byte-deterministic when nothing changes.
extend_regime_labels uses the rule-based adaptive gate (vvix_threshold=None). The C21 fix in cloud_refresh itself is correct; the gap is in app.py (reported separately).
The test suite in a private copy gives 642 passed, 24 skipped, and tests modify no tracked files.
The Procfile's gunicorn command boots and serves 200s.
numpy 1.26.4 (the requirements floor) loads the bot-written joint_cal_2026-09-11.pkl despite its numpy._core references, so the numpy floor is not a pickle hazard.
tests.yml uses least-privilege permissions (contents: read), has a 20-minute timeout, and installs CPU-only torch.
The timeout-minutes: 20 budget is adequate: the observed job takes about 170 s, and calibration alone takes 8-25 s.
